solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dissolution of reason infuses wicked behaviour (13)

indicators.note: dissolving something breaks it up, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A moralist warns that once reason breaks down, wickedness seeps in.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sermon on reason giving way to vice; in fact 'infuses' is only fodder, and all thirteen letters of 'reason infuses' are used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'nefarious' means villainous, and the -ness ending makes it the noun for villainous conduct.

clue.text: HP Lovecraft’s first piece with an imaginary universe? (5-5,4)

indicators.note: Lovecraft's first letter is L

blocks.note: HP is hire purchase, known informally in Britain as the never-never
the first letter of Lovecraft
with = and

annotation.surface: A reader wonders whether an H. P. Lovecraft story opened with its own invented cosmos.
annotation.walkthrough: HP looks like the horror writer's initials, but it is split off as hire purchase: British slang calls buying on instalments 'the never-never'.
annotation.definitionFit: Never-never land is Peter Pan's fantasy land, so any imaginary realm; the question mark flags the loose 'universe'.

clue.text: Fails miserably following cuts (5)

blocks.note: f. is the abbreviation for following
to lop is to cut off

annotation.surface: Budget cuts are blamed for an organisation failing badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Following cuts' reads as 'after cuts', but 'following' simply supplies F, the abbreviation used in page references.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used especially of shows and films that close quickly or lose money.

clue.text: Game reprobate set up involves endless change (4,6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting a word up writes it bottom to top
the reversed word takes the next piece inside it
the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a reprobate is a sinner; turned upward it is RENNIS
ALTER without its final letter, placed inside RENNIS after RE

annotation.surface: A scoundrel is setting up a game that involves constant change.
annotation.walkthrough: Real tennis is the old indoor court game from which lawn tennis descends.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the original indoor racket sport, played in walled courts such as Hampton Court's, from which lawn tennis took its name.

clue.text: Perhaps second stage of infancy is filled with much noise (7)

indicators.note: the first piece has the second placed inside it

blocks.note: in Freud's scheme the oral stage is the first stage of infancy
a din is a lot of noise; it goes inside OR…AL

annotation.surface: A parent notices that the second phase of a baby's life is full of racket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second stage of infancy' pretends to be one phrase; 'Perhaps second' is the definition and 'stage of infancy' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Second is an example of an ordinal number, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Temporarily stop rise of American disbursement (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that rises reads bottom to top

blocks.note: US = American, turned upward to SU
a spend is an outlay of money

annotation.surface: Someone calls for a halt to rising American spending.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rise of American disbursement' reads as growing US spending; 'rise' in fact acts only on the two-letter abbreviation for American.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a meeting or a player can be halted for a while, with a return expected.

clue.text: Former city CEO? (4)

blocks.note: ex = former
EC is the postcode for the City of London

annotation.surface: A former City chief executive is described in two words.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an ex-chief executive, but the answer is a current one; the question mark marks the CEO as one kind of exec.
annotation.definitionFit: A CEO is a chief executive, and an exec is an executive.

clue.text: Might you wind up helping yourself to this? (9)

definitions.text: Might you wind up helping yourself to this?

blocks.note: the surface pushes 'end up', as in finishing somewhere; the setter means literally winding, twirling something round and round
the surface suggests taking something greedily; the setter means serving yourself a helping of food, long strands of pasta twirled on a fork

annotation.surface: It sounds like a warning about ending up somewhere through greed or self-help.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' reads as 'end up'; here it is literal, the twirling of pasta round a fork.
annotation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is the food you literally wind up to eat.

clue.text: Agreement in writing (14)

blocks.note: when two accounts match point for point, they agree
letters written to one another

annotation.surface: A deal is put down on paper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Agreement in writing' looks like a contract; it is two separate senses of the one word.
annotation.definitionFit: Correspondence means both a matching agreement and an exchange of letters.

clue.text: Regularly avoid only a low-sounding instrument (5)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, here every second one

blocks.note: the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of AVOIDONLYA

annotation.surface: Advice to shun everything except one deep-toned instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low-sounding' belongs to the definition: this is the alto of the string family, deeper than the violin.
annotation.definitionFit: The viola is pitched below the violin, so it is a lower-sounding instrument.

clue.text: Outlaw, finally arrested, sure makes a fuss (9)

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of the next words

blocks.note: the last letters of arrested, sure and makes
a = per, as in 'twice a day'
ado = fuss

annotation.surface: A captured outlaw kicks up a fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finally arrested' reads as the outlaw at last being caught; 'finally' actually applies to three words, and 'a' must be read as 'per'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a reckless, violent criminal of Wild West stories, from an old Spanish word for 'desperate'.

clue.text: Optimistic Tories tend to be disordered (4-6)

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A jibe that hopeful Conservatives are usually chaotic.
annotation.walkthrough: Tories are the British Conservative Party.
annotation.definitionFit: Seeing through rose-tinted glasses means being optimistic.

clue.text: Divine figure, somewhat authoritarian (4)

indicators.note: only some of the next word is used

blocks.note: the four letters that follow the opening AU

annotation.surface: A god described as a bit of a tyrant.
annotation.walkthrough: The Norse thunder god sits in au-THOR-itarian; 'somewhat' reads as 'rather' in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse god of thunder.

clue.text: Ace cake provided by ball’s hosts (10)

blocks.note: A = ace, as on playing cards
a bun is a small cake
a ball is a dance; ball's = dance is, contracted to DANCES

annotation.surface: A great cake is supplied by the people hosting a ball.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hosts' looks like the people giving the ball; it is the noun meaning multitudes, as in 'a host of'.
annotation.definitionFit: A host is a great number, as is an abundance.

clue.text: Select from list untrustworthy person receiving mass censure (7)

indicators.note: the first word takes the others inside it

blocks.note: someone slippery is an eel
m = mass
to pan is to criticise harshly; M + PAN go inside E…EL

annotation.surface: A shady figure on a shortlist faces a wave of criticism.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mass censure' reads as a public outcry, but 'mass' is only its one-letter abbreviation, set before the censure.
annotation.definitionFit: To empanel a jury is to choose its members from a list.

clue.text: Do protein shakes split when served? (9)

indicators.note: the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A gym-goer asks whether protein shakes get divided up when handed out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Protein shakes' looks like the drink, but 'shakes' is a verb telling you to shake up DO PROTEIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Food that is portioned is divided up into servings.

clue.text: Group lying maybe about discussions (7)

indicators.note: 'about' can mean turned round, as in 'about turn', so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: a set is a group
abed means in bed, where one may be lying

annotation.surface: A gathering of liars, perhaps, is the subject of talks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests telling fibs; it is lying down, i.e. abed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: formal arguments in which both sides are heard.

clue.text: What line is taken by productive biologist? (7)

indicators.note: the line is taken into the next word

blocks.note: eh? = what?
rich soil is productive
l = line; it goes inside RICH to make RLICH

annotation.surface: A question about what method a prolific scientist adopted.
annotation.walkthrough: The question 'What line…' is the wordplay itself: 'What' is EH. Paul Ehrlich was the German Nobel-winning pioneer of chemotherapy.
annotation.definitionFit: Paul Ehrlich was a biologist and medical scientist.

clue.text: Try hard, after voicing enthusiasm up front in the past (4,1,2)

indicators.note: take the letter at the front of each word

blocks.note: the first letters of hard, after, voicing, enthusiasm
ago = in the past

annotation.surface: Someone recalls making a strong effort after cheering loudly long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Try hard' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Try' and 'hard' is the first of four words whose initials give HAVE.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to take a shot at something you may fail at, which is exactly what trying means.

clue.text: One attempt to track advanced skin condition (7)

blocks.note: money advanced is lent
I = one
a go is an attempt

annotation.surface: A single try at tracing how a skin complaint progressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advanced' tempts as a late-stage illness, but it means paid ahead, as with a loan; 'to track' means the one-attempt pair comes after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Lentigo is a skin condition of small brown spots, such as freckles.

clue.text: Light from back of vessel followed by an aquatic bird (7)

indicators.note: take the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: the last letter of vessel
used as it stands
a tern is a seabird

annotation.surface: A lamp shines from a ship's stern and a seabird trails behind.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a stern lamp; 'back of vessel' in fact takes only the final letter of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one kind of light, a lamp inside a protective glass case.

clue.text: Put part of old radio back (4)

indicators.note: to go back is to return the way you came, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: old radios were tuned with a dial

annotation.surface: Someone asks for a component of a vintage radio to be refitted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put back' reads as 'replace'; 'Put' is the past tense definition and 'back' turns DIAL round.
annotation.definitionFit: Laid, like put, is the past tense of placing something down.

clue.text: Worker made matching boxes for fair (4-6)

indicators.note: the second word encloses the first

blocks.note: to even things is to make them match
a hand is a worker; it goes inside EVEN…ED

annotation.surface: A factory hand produced matching cartons for a fair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' and 'fair' conjure a funfair stall's packaging; 'boxes' is a verb and 'fair' means just.
annotation.definitionFit: Even-handed means treating all sides fairly.

clue.text: Two numbers covered by The White Stripes? I haven’t the foggiest! (5)

indicators.note: the numbers go inside the next word

blocks.note: the White Stripes were a two-piece rock band
n = number, twice; placed inside DU…O

annotation.surface: Asked which two songs the White Stripes covered, someone admits total ignorance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' and 'covered' look like songs and cover versions; here numbers are the letter N and covered means enclosed.
annotation.definitionFit: Dunno, a slurred 'don't know', means I haven't the foggiest.

clue.text: Requests things to do, but with no time (4)

indicators.note: remove the letter that follows

blocks.note: tasks are things to do
t = time, removed from TASKS

annotation.surface: Someone has a to-do list but no time to deal with it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a busy person's lament; 'no time' is an instruction to drop the one-letter abbreviation for time.
annotation.definitionFit: Asks, like requests, is a plural noun for things sought.

clue.text: When adjusted, a lens can start to observe at the very finest level (9)

definitions.note: NANOSCALE is an adjective; the definition is an adverbial phrase, as in 'working nanoscale'

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged
take the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
the first letter of observe, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A microscopist explains that a lens, once adjusted, can see the tiniest detail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the surface's verb, but it is part of the fodder; every word from 'a' to 'can' is shuffled.
annotation.definitionFit: Nanoscale describes things measured in billionths of a metre, the very finest level.

clue.text: Standard chapter by mystery writer? (5)

blocks.note: c = chapter
Anon, short for anonymous, is the writer whose identity is a mystery

annotation.surface: A benchmark chapter written by a crime novelist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mystery writer' suggests a detective novelist; it is the unknown author credited as Anon.
annotation.definitionFit: A canon is a standard or rule by which things are judged.

clue.text: Criminal cons tourist to enter extremely desirable shop (8,5)

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged, as a criminal twists things
the anagram goes inside the next piece
take the outer letters of the next word

blocks.note: the first and last letters of desirable
anagram of CONS TOURIST, placed between D and E

annotation.surface: A crook swindles a visitor into going into a very pleasant shop.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a tourist scam; 'Criminal' is the anagram signal, not the swindler.
annotation.definitionFit: A discount store is a shop selling at reduced prices.
